title: [Lean] Verify one literal PR442 invocation against the multi-host contract
body:
Upstream has incorporated #442 and the #509/#516 abstract stream-model results. This contribution checks concrete obligations for one literal PR442 R747 invocation: stage 2, replica 0, pair 0 at commit 4e16d001d505d4f21dd2bcfc44591f9be4c279bd.

Task A generalizes the hosting contract to multiple hosts and recovers the single-host theorems. Task B connects the selected 19,002-instruction word to that contract, with Lean certificates for scalar endpoints, concrete ownership, coordinate identities and COPY/ERASE guards, for arbitrary dirty Boolean helpers and one explicitly clean, restored private temporary.

Merged #516 already proves abstract realization for arbitrary global state under hypotheses. This contribution checks selected concrete invocation obligations in Lean; it is not the first arbitrary-state theorem. The overlap review covers incorporated #509/#516 and draft #528:
https://github.com/cheesegrader/integer-mult-bounds/blob/lean/pr442-invocation-review/research/lean-external-review/MERGED-OVERLAP.md

Main declarations include MultiHosting.multi_hosting, MultiHosting.SingleHost.whole_hosting_recovered, MultiHosting.SingleHost.physical_whole_hosting_recovered, SourceInvocation.actualContract, SourceInvocation.selected_call_completion, SourceInvocation.selected_native_completion, SourceInvocation.selected_native_realization, and SourceInvocation.selected_temporary_restoration.

Both tasks PASSED fresh without resume. Task A compiled six modules and audited 21 declarations. Task B compiled all 52 modules and audited 931 declarations, including SourceInvocation.actualContract. No project modules were reused. Task B completed at 2026-10-12 03:19:37 UTC.

The fresh receipt matches the current manifest and records unchanged installed toolchain/library fingerprints before and after compilation. The replay used pinned, fingerprinted Lean/Mathlib dependencies; it does not claim a fresh Mathlib rebuild or a leanchecker --fresh audit of the complete imported environment.

Task B receipt:
https://github.com/cheesegrader/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c4b1560a569f54064608bf88440f9e492c03fba3/research/lean-external-review/validation/task-b.json

Source extraction, strict package verification, and exported patch/archive validation also passed. All 75 included Lean source files remain unchanged.

After completing the dependency setup, reproduce with:

python3 research/lean-external-review/reproduce.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.33.0-linux/bin/lean --mathlib /path/to/mathlib4 --build-dir /tmp/review-task-b-fresh --receipt-dir /tmp/review-receipts-fresh

Dependency setup and package instructions:
https://github.com/cheesegrader/integer-mult-bounds/blob/lean/pr442-invocation-review/research/lean-external-review/README.md

The upstream base is db0e57bc7f36b5ac0fc844ad7ce1396165ee6647. This package uses Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d. Upstream #509/#516 use Lean 4.21.0 and Mathlib 308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3. No port is included.

Scope limitations:

- One complete invocation; cross-invocation disjointness is not exercised.
- Pending ranges 15..21 and 1..28 are hand-supplied. Lean checks target-mask containment; nothing binds them to the source schedule.
- Explicit input embeddings, an invertible chart and 2 ≠ 0 are required. Source extraction is externally checked Python. Original-bank outputs remain auxiliary state.
- No full sweep, later scheduling, global-allocation equivalence, costs, all-size compilation, analytic transfer or κ result is proved. PR448’s gain remains unestablished. PR493 → PR472 → PR442 is provenance only.

Original construction and predecessor credits remain in the source notices. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The human participant initiated and coordinated the effort and does not claim independent derivation or personal checking of the mathematics. Agent reviews are not human audits.

Questions for maintainers:

1. Do the literal source binding, slot isometries, native operations and private initialization faithfully represent this invocation?
2. Is retaining all host/data/exterior outputs with explicit auxiliary bank outputs the right boundary for later scheduling proofs?
3. Where should these concrete certificates integrate with #509/#516 and #528?
4. Is a standalone Lean 4.33 package acceptable, or is a 4.21 port required?
